title: Microsoft Teams: allowed list of external meeting notetaker bots
summary: Hold: the briefing says meeting policies determine what an allowed bot can hear or record, but Microsoft has not documented that protection for the planned list. The roadmap facts, existing bot-management control and its command are supported; the recording statement should be narrowed to the roadmap's promise of appropriate meeting-policy enforcement.

claims.claim: Existing Teams bot detection uses signals collected during the meeting join process.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process.

claims.claim: With existing bot detection enabled, detected bots are placed in the lobby irrespective of the meeting's lobby configuration.
claims.quote: The participants detected as bots are placed in the meeting lobby irrespective of the lobby configuration for the meeting.

claims.claim: Detected bots require explicit admission into the meeting.
claims.quote: Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.

claims.claim: The external-bots guide says presenters can also admit detected bots depending on the meeting setting.
claims.quote: Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.

claims.claim: The Bot Identification Program page instead describes detected bots as requiring organizer approval.
claims.quote: Even when a meeting allows participants to bypass the lobby, detected bots still require organizer approval before joining.

claims.claim: The existing bot-handling setting defaults to When detected, require approval before joining, represented by RequireApprovalWhenDetected.
claims.quote: | When detected, require approval before joining | RequireApprovalWhenDetected | (default) Bots are detected and marked in the lobby. They're enforced to be in the lobby until explicitly admitted into the meeting. |

claims.claim: What an allowed bot can hear or record in a meeting depends on the meeting policies applied.

claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of Risk assessment > Data exposure with: 'Per the roadmap, an allowed bot is treated like a regular external participant, and meeting policies are enforced as appropriate.' Keep the subsequent transcript-storage caveat and advice to review each bot's data handling. The roadmap does not specify which policies restrict what the bot can hear or record.
